speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing the nosebleeds and skin spots, and have you noticed any bleeding from your gums or heavy menstrual periods if applicable?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child had any recent fevers, joint pain, or bone pain, and have you noticed any swelling in the abdomen or enlarged lymph nodes? Also, is there any family history of bleeding disorders or similar symptoms in siblings?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count with Platelet Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Coagulation Panel: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do the petechiae primarily appear after episodes of crying, vomiting, or straining, and is there a family history of similar bleeding tendencies? I am also checking if the child has experienced any bleeding from the umbilical stump or delayed wound healing.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet Function Assay: Absent platelet aggregation response to ADP, epinephrine, collagen, and ristocetin. Glanzmann Thrombasthenia Workup: ELISA Binding Assay confirms platelet surfaces deficient in GPIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The deficient GPIIb/IIIa receptors and absent aggregation confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia
